Task id: t01_slugify

# Issue #41: `slugify` produces double hyphens and trailing hyphens

`slugify("Hello,  World!")` returns `"hello--world-"` but should return `"hello-world"`.
Also `slugify("--a--b--")` should give `"a-b"`.

Please fix `textkit/slug.py`. Do not change the public signature.

tests/test_slug.py
textkit/__init__.py
textkit/slug.py

1| import re
   2| 
   3| def slugify(text: str) -> str:
   4|     """Turn arbitrary text into a URL slug: lowercase, ASCII letters and
   5|     digits, words separated by single hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphens."""
   6|     text = text.lower()
   7|     text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "-", text)
   8|     return text

print(repr(slugify('--a--b--')))

arguments.summary: Fixed slugify in textkit/slug.py by changing the replacement regex from `[^a-z0-9]` to `[^a-z0-9]+` (collapsing runs of non-alphanumeric characters into a single hyphen) and stripping leading/trailing hyphens with `.strip("-")`. This makes `slugify("Hello,  World!")` return `"hello-world"` and `slugify("--a--b--")` return `"a-b"`; the public signature is unchanged and all tests pass.
